findings.issue_text: [BUG] When a remote's refs/remotes/<r>/HEAD resolves inside its own remote, remoteDefaultRefs stops excluding that remote's main and master, which the previous code always excluded. In a gitflow repo whose origin/HEAD names develop (or one whose origin/HEAD is stale after a master-to-main rename), a branch cut from a fresh origin/main while local main lags takes merged main commits — and their runs and findings — back into its range, the pull-in the exclusion exists to prevent.
[ADVISORY] The comment above Load's remote listing still says the remote defaults are refs/remotes/<remote>/main|master. Readers are told the wrong default-branch rule.

[ADVISORY] internal/status tests obtain an unknown scope from a bare t.TempDir() and assume TMPDIR is outside a repository, as the findings tests did before (e). With TMPDIR inside a checkout, 11 status tests fail; nothing fails in a normal environment.
[ADVISORY] The --all warning wording is swapped in emit() by a string match on a constant built in buildFor. A future rewording can silently keep the self-referential hint.

[ADVISORY] refs/remotes/<r>/HEAD can be pointed at a remote-tracking ref of one's own pushed branch, subtracting it from the range. Legacy range-only rows could fall out of scope; not a new capability (update-ref of refs/remotes/origin/main already does it).
